title: Saturday, 11:40 p.m.
intro: WMRC after the hour. The ON AIR sign is dark. The records cool like old stones.

items.label: Reel: SAT 9/9/61 NOT AIRED
items.text: You thread it. A man's voice, very calm, very fast: '...it's in the square. The water is in the square. Fair water, Mercy. Fair water, every one of you.' The tape ends in a long, clean silence.

items.label: Chapel bulletin file
items.text: A bulletin from 1963: 'Hymn 212 is retired with thanks.' Under it, a note in pencil: 'It was never ours to retire.'

items.label: Emergency transmitter
items.text: A hand-cranked set in a cabinet marked IN CASE. Someone wound it recently. The crank is warm.

items.label: Pencil on the wall
items.text: Behind the filing cabinet, small and neat: FAIR WATER. Below it, the same words in different handwriting, over and over, sixty-three years of them.

items.label: Tape racks
items.text: Eleven thousand tapes of weather, hymns, and one man saying 'And now, the weather' like it was a love letter.

items.label: Cold coffee
items.text: Vern's. Three days old. It's practically a lifestyle.

items.label: The console
items.text: Faders. Dials. A little brass plate: 'Presented to L. Page for services to broadcasting, 1960.'

items.label: ON AIR sign
items.text: Dark. If you flicked it, the whole valley would hear. You could. You decide to think about that.
